subject.title: fix(cli): reject oversized --file input before reading in config patch

question: Should `config patch` gain a documented maximum input size for both `--file` and `--stdin`, and if so what compatibility-safe byte limit should become the public contract?
rationale: Current behavior has no documented 1 MiB ceiling, so selecting that threshold and applying it to only one public input mode is a product and upgrade-compatibility choice rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Define one shared limit
options.body: Approve a documented byte limit for both file and stdin inputs, then implement one bounded reader and test both fresh and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Keep file-only limit
options.body: Intentionally accept and document that file patches above 1 MiB fail while equivalent stdin patches remain accepted.

options.title: Avoid a new cap
options.body: Pause this PR until a resource-bound solution can be designed without changing the accepted config-patch size contract.

recommendation.title: Define one shared limit
recommendation.body: Approve a documented byte limit for both file and stdin inputs, then implement one bounded reader and test both fresh and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice changes the public CLI contract and requires project-level product and compatibility ownership.
